title: Comparison harness vs aff3ct and IT++
description:
## Goal

Side-by-side comparison harness producing AWGN BLER curves for
DVB-T2 r1/2 16-QAM and at least one 5G NR LDPC configuration vs
aff3ct or IT++ on identical channel parameters.

## Context

Task under story `a5635da5` (5G NR + research enablers) within epic
`gf2-sim` (`f9717e7e`). Sequencing: depends on `23d3525f` (5G NR
kernel tuning). Aspirational epic deliverable from `f9717e7e` (the
research-grade story).

aff3ct is a C++ FEC simulation library (https://aff3ct.github.io/);
IT++ (http://itpp.sourceforge.net/) is an older but still-used
research library. Either suffices for an external comparison.

## Deliverables

1. Comparison harness in `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/comparison/`:
   - Driver script: `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/comparison/run.sh`
     (bash) that runs:
     - The gf2-sim LDPC decoder (isolated LDPC-only AWGN-BPSK
       arm, `ldpc_bler_sweep` bin) at a fixed bracket for the
       DVB-T2 r1/2 Normal LDPC code (AMENDMENT 2026-06-12d).
     - aff3ct at the matching configuration via its CLI
       (hermetic pinned-tag build), decoding the identical H
       exported to MacKay AList (`--dec-h-path`), AZCW transmit
       on both sides.
     - Both invocations use the same seed, same channel model,
       and matched per-point frame-error budgets (aff3ct v4.4.0
       has no per-point frame cap — only `-e`; `run.sh` bounds
       each aff3ct point with a timeout).
   - For 5G NR: same comparison for the BG1 / Z=384 mother code
     (rate ~0.323; N=26112, K=8448; AMENDMENT 2026-06-12d).
2. CSV outputs:
   - `comparison/dvb-t2-r12-16qam-vs-aff3ct.csv` with columns:
     `es_n0_db, gf2_sim_bler, aff3ct_bler, gf2_sim_fps,
     aff3ct_fps`.
   - `comparison/nr-5g-bg1-r12-vs-aff3ct.csv` (or `vs-itpp.csv`
     depending on the chosen reference).
3. Visualisation notebook or plot script
   (`dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/comparison/plot.py`) producing
   side-by-side BLER curves (PNG).
4. README at `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/comparison/README.md`
   documenting the reference library version, invocation, host,
   and headline result (BLER agreement within ± 0.2 dB at FER
   10⁻²).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] CSV files for at least one DVB-T2 and one 5G NR
  configuration vs at least one external library (aff3ct or
  IT++) committed under
  `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/comparison/`.
- [hard] BLER curves agree with the external library within
  ± 0.2 dB at FER 10⁻² (any larger discrepancy must be
  investigated and reported in the README before this gate
  passes).
- [hard] PNG plots committed.
- [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review` gates green.

## Non-goals

- This is the [aspirational] epic deliverable; if the external
  library installation is infeasible on the available host,
  document the blocker in the README and escalate. Do not skip
  silently.

## AMENDMENT 2026-06-12d (user-approved)

Deliverable-1 originally specified the full-chain DVB-T2 r1/2
16-QAM comparison "via the campaign binary", NR "BG1 / Z=384 /
r1/2", and "same number of frames per SNR point". Amended to the
landed isolated-decoder comparison because:

- aff3ct cannot express the DVB-T2 BCH outer code or bit
  interleaver, so full-chain-vs-LDPC-only would not be
  apples-to-apples; the LDPC-only AWGN-BPSK arm decodes the
  bit-identical H (SHA-256-pinned AList export) on both sides,
  and AZCW removes the encoder mismatch (aff3ct systematic vs
  gf2-coding RU encoder from the same H).
- 3GPP NR rate matching is gf2-coding-internal LLR bookkeeping
  not expressible to aff3ct through an AList; the BG1 Z=384
  mother code is the exact same-H comparison.
- aff3ct v4.4.0 has only `-e` (frame-error budget), no frame
  cap, so identical per-point frame counts are unimplementable;
  error budgets (200) are matched and `run.sh` bounds each
  aff3ct point with a per-point timeout.

The CSV filenames keep the issue's deliverable names
(`dvb-t2-r12-16qam-vs-aff3ct.csv`, `nr-5g-bg1-r12-vs-aff3ct.csv`);
the README documents that the curves inside are the LDPC-only
comparison. Measured agreement: 0.016 dB (DVB-T2) / 0.003 dB (NR)
at FER 1e-2 — inside the +/- 0.2 dB [hard] criterion. Success
criteria bullets unchanged by this amendment.
